project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will enable Isle au Haut Boat Services to undertake a much needed rebuild of the pier in Stonington, ME. The current pier is deteriorating and must be replaced with a more structurally sound one to improve functionality and reduce maintenance needs. The existing pier also sustained damage after being lifted from its bedrock pins during the January 2024 storms. A fully functional pier is vital to providing this essential service for residents.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to implement needed upgrades at the Gardiner Wastewater Treatment Facility (WWTF) and Maine Avenue Pumping Station (MAPS). These upgrades include a new Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition system (SCADA). The SCADA system uses computer systems and sensors to remotely monitor, control, and automate processes. Upgrades also include screw pump and flow control box water level monitoring, chemical storage tanks, feed pumps with piping, aeration blowers, HVAC improvements, and a partial roof replacement. At the MAPS location, electrical, SCADA, motor control center and generator improvements will be undertaken. These upgrades will greatly improve the overall system's efficiency, extend the life of many critical components, and increase the level of safety for the system's operators, while also helping to preserve the quality of the nearby Kennebec River.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to provide a wide range of technical assistance to towns and/or groups of towns operating together in Androscoggin, Franklin, and Oxford counties, with the goal of reducing the amount of toxicity of disposed waste, improving the resiliency of the local and regional waste systems. This project will enhance efficiencies and reduce costs; increase institutional capacity, compliance, and resiliency; protect the environment and public health; and improve waste reduction, recycling, and reuse. With 17 years of help from Rural Developments the Solid Waste Management Grant program, tax dollars have been saved, local capacity and resiliency have improved, safety and environmental protection has increased, and the amount and toxicity of wastes disposed has been decreased. The recent priorities are handling organics, demolition debris, and conversion to single stream recycling. Municipal officers and site operators also change over time requiring re-education relative to solid waste and recycling processing and procedures.

naics_industry_sector: Other or Not Defined
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to obtain funding for Fish River Rural Health, a non-profit, federally qualified community health center, successfully operating for over 30 years. They provide primary care, dental, optometry, chiropractic care, telehealth medicine and food distribution services. They serve the northern most towns in Aroostook County in the St. John Valley area. The COVID-19 pandemic exacerbated the inequity for rural residents and was compounded by the Canadian border closure. Most border community residents have historically crossed the U.S. and Canadian border for dental and optometry services. Since March of 2020, they have seen an increase of 100 rural residents being seen, per month, at this facility. The primary purpose of the grant is to support Fish River Rural Health in their continued efforts to diagnose and manage COVID-19 and other future pandemics throughout the Northern Aroostook County communities.This will be achieved by purchasing the necessary equipment for family medicine, dental, optometry services, along with technology and food distribution services as they relate to COVID-19.

naics_industry_sector: Health Care and Social Assistance
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to purchase an ambulance. The project focuses on an important equipment investment to address needs for access to health care services that have been intensified by the COVID-19 pandemic and future pandemics. More patients are needing medical transport to facilities that have the capacity to care for them. Ambulances also have more out-of-service time as they are thoroughly cleaned between runs. An additional ambulance will expand transport capacity for Piscataquis County. MRH Corp. currently performs 3,500-4,000 transports per year out of its three bases. The main base in Dover-Foxcroft is the largest. The pandemic and the high positivity rate in Piscataquis County have increased the transport volume of U-121 patients (those exhibiting COVID-19 symptoms). COVID-19 has also increased out-of-service time for ambulances as they are rigorously cleaned between runs. Transport of U-121 patients is markedly more complex than usual, requiring full personal protective equipment of the staff as well as respirators and face shields. State of the art, well-functioning equipment is necessary for the support of the staff and comfort of the patient.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to install a 600 cubic-foot freezer and a 48-kilowatt propane powered backup generator. Piscataquis Regional Food Center receives and redistributes 650,000 - 800,000 pounds of food per year from Good Shepherd Food Bank to 14 local food pantries. They also make deliveries to eligible house-bound seniors in the region. A critical component of Piscataquis Regional Food Centers ability to meet the communitys needs is the capacity to safely store food products in frozen, refrigerated, and shelf-stable forms until they can be delivered to rural distribution partners or direct to those in need. This requires a reliable and uninterrupted year-round source of electricity. Without backup power, their ability to support their community is at risk if there is any significant grid power disruption. The COVID-19 emergency demonstrated the rural regions need for food assistance can dramatically increase in scope with almost no warning. Current capacity was put under great stress for a prolonged period as the volume of frozen foods increased significantly for several months, disproportionate to refrigerated and shelf-stable products. More than a year later, they are still seeing unusually high frozen food storage needs relative to pre-COVID-19 conditions.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to propose a two-pronged solid waste management project which addresses low recycling rates and an urgent per-and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS)contamination challenge. The project seeks to increase recycling rates to 50% for eight targeted municipalities, and plans to do so by expanding conventional recycling, food, textile, and household hazardous waste diversion. Since their service region is one of the nations PFAS contamination hot spots, they propose to provide technical assistance to municipalities for the assessment of PFAS in the waste stream and regional coordination of treatment options. Through their participation in technical assistance and recycling programs, these eight municipalities will derive measurable financial benefit and improved environmental quality and public health outcomes. Domestic infrastructure for recycled materials is lucrative and premium recycled materials are in high-demand; yet, small rural municipalities have not benefited from this growing market because they have no recycling centers or no process for separating recyclables.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used for a Special Evaluation Assistance for Rural Communities and Household grant to conduct an Engineering Study of its current wastewater System to include evaluating the treatment lagoons and overall system, the spray irrigation pump station and controls, and the pumping stations in the collection system. The applicant is a quasi-municipal district and provides wastewater collection and treatment services to rural residents in Eagle Lake, Maine. The existing system is approximately 36 years old and many components are reaching the end of their useful life. The Study of the existing conditions of the wastewater system will be used to identify needed improvements and identify and evaluate alternatives. Upon completion of the study, the District will be ready to implement the recommended improvements to improve the facilities over all treatment process to meet EPAs discharge requirements.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to provide business based training and technical assistance to rural microborrowers and potential microborrowers throughout Lincoln, Knox, and Sagadahoc Counties as well as Brunswick and Harpswell in Cumberland County and Searsmont, Belmont, Northport, and Lincolnville in Waldo County. project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to continue providing a wide range of technical assistance to towns and/or groups of towns operating together in the three-county region of Androscoggin, Franklin, and Oxford, with the goal of reducing the amount of toxicity of waste being disposed and continuing to improve the sustainability of the local and regional solid waste systems. To accomplish this goal, Androscoggin Valley Council of Governments will work with communities to improve efficiencies, reduce costs were possible, protect the environment and public health, increase institutional capacity and compliance, and ensure adequate facilities for now and the future. With 15 years of assistance from Rural Developments Solid Waste Management Grant program, tax dollars have been saved, safety and environmental protection have increased, and the amount and toxicity of wastes disposed has been decreased. Waste handling and processing technologies are ever changing, requiring everyone to be apprised of new technologies, market conditions, cost increases, and new opportunities. The most recent priorities have been: handling organics (food scrap composting), demolition debris, and conversion to single stream recycling. Municipal officers and site operators also change over time requiring re-education relative to solid waste and recycling processing and procedures.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to offer public education, municipal training, and environmentally sound disposal opportunities for household hazardous waste for small towns in Maine. This project will provide specific technical assistance towards the 14 small communities with the lowest incomes and will respond to the evolving solid waste management needs of this rural region in a flexible, yet focused manner. Program A will provide education, planning and assistance with the collection and environmentally responsible disposal of household hazardous waste for small towns in the region. This is accomplished by organizing collection events, drafting requests for proposals, providing towns with educational brochures, press releases, and contract negotiation services. Program B will provide technical training and outreach on current solid waste management and waste reduction, such as the training of transfer station and public works staff on licensing and environmental regulation compliance, hazardous waste exclusion, and waste stream reduction practices including recycling and composting. Program C will provide staff time to continue assisting municipalities with a variety of technical help with topics such as waste reduction through organics composting, recycling, product stewardship, and planning for new municipal disposal systems that will protect the environment and comply with regulations.
